statement: For a finite simple perfect graph G and every nonnegative node-weight vector w, the maximum-weight stable-set value equals the weighted fractional clique-cover optimum.
assumptions: G is perfect, meaning every induced subgraph H satisfies chi(H) = omega(H)
w is a nonnegative real vector indexed by V(G)
reported_primary_source: V. Chvatal, On certain polytopes associated with graphs (1975)
kernel_proves: Only consequences derived after receiving this weighted-duality statement as an explicit hypothesis.
kernel_does_not_prove: the Chvatal weighted perfect-graph theorem itself
that an arbitrary graph is perfect
that finite-instance graph checks establish the universal theorem
unexpanded_scope: The target paper locally derives its clean antiblocker identity from this weighted duality plus downward closure. The prototype does not import that cleaner target-local statement as though a cited primary source had stated it verbatim.
